scripts.title: Weather changer
scripts.where: Put this Script in ServerScriptService (add the Rain, Snow and Thunderstorm scripts to see the weather).
scripts.about: Picks new random weather every few minutes (Clear, Rain, Storm or Snow) and tells everyone through a Workspace attribute.
scripts.code:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

-- Settings: weather and how often each happens (bigger = more often)
local WEATHER = {
	{ name = "Clear", weight = 50, fogEnd = 100000 },
	{ name = "Rain", weight = 25, fogEnd = 600 },
	{ name = "Storm", weight = 10, fogEnd = 300 },
	{ name = "Snow", weight = 15, fogEnd = 400 },
}
local CHANGE_EVERY = 180 -- seconds

local function pick()
	local total = 0
	for _, w in ipairs(WEATHER) do
		total += w.weight
	end
	local roll = math.random() * total
	for _, w in ipairs(WEATHER) do
		roll -= w.weight
		if roll <= 0 then
			return w
		end
	end
	return WEATHER[1]
end

while true do
	local weather = pick()
	workspace:SetAttribute("Weather", weather.name) -- client scripts read this
	-- Fog closes in for bad weather (only works if Lighting has no Atmosphere object)
	TweenService:Create(Lighting, TweenInfo.new(10), { FogEnd = weather.fogEnd }):Play()
	task.wait(CHANGE_EVERY)
end

scripts.title: 8 LEDs from 3 Pins (74HC595 Shift Register)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 74HC595: DS (pin 14) to Arduino 11, SHCP (pin 11) to 12, STCP (pin 12) to 8, MR (10) to 5V, OE (13) to GND, VCC (16) 5V, GND (8); 8 LEDs on Q0 to Q7 with 220 ohm resistors.
scripts.about: Uses a 74HC595 chip to control 8 LEDs with just 3 Arduino pins and plays a few light patterns.

scripts.title: 8x8 LED Matrix Faces (MAX7219)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LedControl" by Eberhard Fahle; MAX7219 module DIN to 12, CLK to 11, CS to 10, VCC 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Shows a smiley, a heart and a surprised face on an 8x8 LED matrix.

scripts.title: AA Battery Tester
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; battery + to A0, battery - to GND (only 1.5V AA, AAA or 1 cell, never more than 5V); green LED 4, yellow LED 5, red LED 6 with 220 ohm resistors.
scripts.about: Measures a 1.5 V battery and lights green, yellow or red to show if it is good, ok or dead.

scripts.title: Air Piano (Ultrasonic Theremin)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; HC-SR04 Trig to pin 9, Echo to pin 10; passive buzzer on pin 8. Move your hand 5 to 40 cm above the sensor.
scripts.about: Plays a note from a scale depending on how far your hand is from the ultrasonic sensor.

scripts.title: ASCII Table Printer
scripts.where: Any Arduino; open Serial Monitor at 9600, then type any key to see its number.
scripts.about: Prints every letter and symbol with its number in decimal, hex and binary, then tells you the code of any key you type.

scripts.title: Automatic Plant Watering Pump
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; soil sensor AO to A0; relay IN to pin 7 driving a small 5V water pump on its own battery pack; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Waters a plant with a pump for a few seconds whenever the soil gets too dry.

scripts.title: Binary Counter with 8 LEDs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 8 LEDs with 220 ohm resistors on pins 2 to 9 (pin 2 is the smallest bit); open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Counts from 0 to 255 and shows each number in binary on 8 LEDs.

scripts.title: Blink an LED
scripts.where: Paste this into a new sketch in the Arduino IDE and upload it to your board. Uses the built-in LED, so no wiring needed.
scripts.about: Turns the board's LED on and off every second.

scripts.title: Blink Two LEDs at Different Speeds
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LED A with 220 ohm resistor on pin 8, LED B on pin 9.
scripts.about: Blinks one LED every 250 ms and another every 1000 ms at the same time, using millis() instead of delay().

scripts.title: Bluetooth Phone Controlled Car
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; HC-05 or HC-06 TXD to pin 2, RXD to pin 3 through a voltage divider (1k and 2k), VCC 5V, GND; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6. Use a phone app like "Arduino Bluetooth RC Car" that sends F, B, L, R, S.
scripts.about: Drives a robot car from a phone app that sends letters like F for forward and S for stop over Bluetooth.

scripts.title: Breathing LED (Sleep Light)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 9 and GND.
scripts.about: Makes an LED gently pulse like a sleeping laptop light, using a sine wave for a smooth look.

scripts.title: Button Interrupt Counter
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; push button between pin 2 and GND (pins 2 and 3 are the Uno's interrupt pins); open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Uses an interrupt so a button press is caught instantly even while the main loop is busy with a long delay.

scripts.title: Button Turns On an LED
scripts.where: Paste this into a new Arduino IDE sketch and upload it; wire one leg of a push button to pin 2 and the other leg to GND, and use the built-in LED.
scripts.about: Each press of the button flips the LED on or off, with debounce so one press counts once.

scripts.title: Buzzer Melody
scripts.where: Paste this into a new Arduino IDE sketch and upload it; wire the buzzer's + leg to pin 8 and the - leg to GND.
scripts.about: Plays "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star" on a buzzer, then waits and plays it again.

scripts.title: Color Sensor TCS3200
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; TCS3200/TCS230 module S0 to 4, S1 to 5, S2 to 6, S3 to 7, OUT to 8, VCC 5V, GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Measures red, green and blue light with a TCS3200 and guesses which color is in front of it.

scripts.title: Control an LED from Your Phone (Bluetooth)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; HC-05/HC-06 TXD to pin 10, RXD to pin 11 through a 1k/2k voltage divider, VCC 5V, GND; LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 9. Use a Bluetooth terminal app on an Android phone.
scripts.about: Type 1 to turn the LED on, 0 to turn it off, or a letter a to j to set its brightness from your phone.

scripts.title: Control LEDs with a TV Remote
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "IRremote" (version 4+); IR receiver OUT to pin 11; LEDs with 220 ohm resistors on pins 4, 5 and 6. Change the codes to match your remote (use the code finder sketch).
scripts.about: Turns three LEDs on and off with buttons 1, 2 and 3 on an infrared remote and button 0 turns all off.

scripts.title: Count How Many Times the Arduino Started
scripts.where: Any Arduino Uno or Nano; open Serial Monitor at 9600, then press the reset button a few times.
scripts.about: Saves a counter in EEPROM memory so it remembers how many times the board has started, even after unplugging it.

scripts.title: DC Motor Speed with a Transistor
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; small DC motor: + to battery +, - to the drain of an IRLZ44N MOSFET (or collector of a TIP120); gate/base to pin 9 through 220 ohm; source/emitter to GND; diode 1N4001 across the motor; join battery - to Arduino GND; knob on A0.
scripts.about: Controls a small DC motor's speed with a knob using a transistor and PWM.

scripts.title: DC Motor with L298N
scripts.where: Paste this into a new Arduino IDE sketch and upload it; wire L298N ENA to pin 9, IN1 to pin 8, IN2 to pin 7, the motor to OUT1 and OUT2, a battery pack to 12V and GND, and the L298N GND to the Arduino GND.
scripts.about: Spins a DC motor forward, then backward, speeding up and slowing down with analogWrite.

scripts.title: Debounced Toggle Button
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; push button between pin 2 and GND; LED on pin 13 (built in); open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Shows how to debounce a button with millis() so one press always counts as exactly one press.

scripts.title: DHT11 Temperature and Humidity
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "DHT sensor library" by Adafruit; DHT11 data pin to pin 2 (with a 10k resistor to 5V if it is a bare sensor), + to 5V, - to GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Reads the temperature and humidity from a DHT11 every two seconds and prints them.

scripts.title: DHT22 Weather Display on an LCD
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "DHT sensor library" and "LiquidCrystal I2C"; DHT22 data to pin 2, LCD I2C SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC to 5V, GND to GND.
scripts.about: Shows the temperature and humidity from a DHT22 on a 16x2 I2C LCD screen.

scripts.title: Ding Dong Doorbell
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; push button between pin 2 and GND; passive buzzer on pin 8; LED on pin 13.
scripts.about: Plays a ding-dong chime and flashes a light when someone presses the doorbell button.

scripts.title: Distance LED Bar Graph
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; HC-SR04 Trig to A0, Echo to A1; 6 LEDs (with 220 ohm resistors) on pins 2 to 7.
scripts.about: Lights up more LEDs the closer your hand gets to the ultrasonic sensor.

scripts.title: Door Open Alarm with a Reed Switch
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; magnetic reed switch (door sensor) between pin 2 and GND, magnet on the door; buzzer on pin 8; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Tells you when a door opens and beeps if it is left open for more than 10 seconds.

scripts.title: Double Clap Light Switch
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; sound sensor module (KY-038 or similar) DO to pin 2, VCC 5V, GND; LED (220 ohm) or relay IN on pin 9. Turn the sensor's screw until its light only blinks on loud sounds.
scripts.about: Turns a light on or off when you clap twice quickly.

scripts.title: DS18B20 Waterproof Temperature Probe
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "OneWire" and "DallasTemperature"; DS18B20 yellow (data) to pin 4, red to 5V, black to GND, and a 4.7k resistor between data and 5V.
scripts.about: Reads the temperature from a waterproof DS18B20 probe, great for fish tanks and drinks.

scripts.title: Electronic Dice on a 7-Segment Display
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; common cathode 7-segment, segments a to g on pins 2 to 8 (220 ohm each), common to GND; button between pin 10 and GND; buzzer on pin 11.
scripts.about: Press the button to roll: the numbers spin fast, slow down and stop on a random 1 to 6.

scripts.title: Fade an LED Up and Down
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LED long leg through a 220 ohm resistor to pin 9, short leg to GND.
scripts.about: Slowly brightens an LED and then dims it again, over and over, using PWM.

scripts.title: Feels-Like Temperature (Heat Index)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "DHT sensor library" by Adafruit; DHT22 or DHT11 data to pin 2; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Uses temperature and humidity to work out how hot it really feels and gives a comfort message.

scripts.title: Find Your IR Remote's Button Codes
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "IRremote" by Armin Joachimsmeyer (version 4 or newer); IR receiver (VS1838B) OUT to pin 11, VCC 5V, GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Prints the code of every button you press on an infrared remote so you can use them in other projects.

scripts.title: Firefly Jar LEDs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 6 yellow-green LEDs with 220 ohm resistors on the PWM pins 3, 5, 6, 9, 10 and 11; put them in a jar for a firefly lamp.
scripts.about: Makes LEDs glow up and fade out at random times like fireflies in a jar.

scripts.title: Flame Detector Alarm
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; IR flame sensor module DO to pin 2, AO to A0, VCC 5V, GND; buzzer pin 8; red LED pin 13. Test only with a candle and an adult nearby.
scripts.about: Sounds an alarm when the flame sensor sees fire and prints how strong it is.

scripts.title: Force Sensor Squeeze Meter
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; FSR (force sensitive resistor) from 5V to A0, with a 10k resistor from A0 to GND; LED on pin 9; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Measures how hard you press the force sensor and makes an LED glow brighter the harder you squeeze.

scripts.title: Four Button Piano
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 4 push buttons from pins 2, 3, 4, 5 to GND; passive buzzer + to pin 8, - to GND.
scripts.about: Turns four buttons into piano keys that play C, D, E and G while you hold them.

scripts.title: Guess the Number in Serial Monitor
scripts.where: Any Arduino; open Serial Monitor at 9600 and set the line ending to "Newline"; type guesses and press Enter.
scripts.about: The Arduino picks a number from 1 to 100 and tells you higher or lower until you guess it.

scripts.title: Happy Birthday Song
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; passive buzzer + to pin 8, - to GND; push button between pin 2 and GND to play it.
keywords: play a tune on button press
scripts.about: Plays Happy Birthday on a buzzer each time you press the button.

scripts.title: Hot Potato Party Game
scripts.where: Arduino Uno (on a battery so you can pass it around); passive buzzer on pin 8; LED on pin 13; button pin 2 to GND starts a round.
scripts.about: Press start and pass the Arduino around while it ticks; whoever holds it when it explodes is out.

scripts.title: I2C Address Scanner
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; connect your I2C device SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC and GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Searches every I2C address and prints which ones have a device, so you know your LCD or sensor address.

scripts.title: Keypad Password Lock
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Keypad"; keypad rows to pins 9, 8, 7, 6 and columns to 5, 4, 3, 2; servo on pin 10; buzzer on A0; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Opens a servo lock when you type the secret code and press #, and buzzes for a wrong code.

scripts.title: Kitchen Countdown Timer
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "TM1637" by Avishay Orpaz; display CLK 2, DIO 3, VCC 5V, GND; potentiometer middle leg on A0 sets minutes; start button pin 4 to GND; buzzer pin 8.
scripts.about: Turn the knob to pick 1 to 60 minutes, press start, and it counts down in mm:ss and beeps at zero.

scripts.title: Knight Rider LED Chaser
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 8 LEDs, each with a 220 ohm resistor, on pins 2 to 9; potentiometer middle leg on A0 sets the speed.
scripts.about: Makes a light zoom back and forth along 8 LEDs, and a knob changes the speed.

scripts.title: L298N Two Motor Test
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; L298N ENA to 5, IN1 to 7, IN2 to 8, IN3 to 9, IN4 to 10, ENB to 6 (remove the ENA/ENB jumpers); motors on OUT1/2 and OUT3/4; battery to 12V and GND, GND joined to Arduino.
scripts.about: Tests a two-motor robot base by driving forward, backward, turning left and right, then stopping.

scripts.title: Lamp that Remembers its Brightness
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 9; button between pin 2 and GND. Unplug and plug back in: it keeps its setting.
scripts.about: Each button press changes the lamp brightness, and the choice is saved in EEPROM so it comes back after power off.

scripts.title: Laser Tripwire Alarm
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; laser module S to pin 7 (never point at eyes); photoresistor 5V to A0 with 10k from A0 to GND, aimed at the laser; buzzer on pin 8; button pin 2 to GND to reset.
scripts.about: Shines a laser at a light sensor and sounds the alarm when someone breaks the beam.

scripts.title: LCD 16x2 I2C Hello World
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LiquidCrystal I2C" by Frank de Brabander; LCD backpack GND to GND, VCC to 5V, SDA to A4, SCL to A5. Turn the blue screw on the back if you see no text.
scripts.about: Shows a message on the top line of an I2C LCD and counts seconds on the bottom line.

scripts.title: LCD 16x2 Without I2C (Parallel Wiring)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LCD RS to 12, E to 11, D4 to 5, D5 to 4, D6 to 3, D7 to 2, RW to GND, VSS GND, VDD 5V, V0 to a 10k pot middle leg, A to 5V via 220 ohm, K to GND.
scripts.about: Uses the built-in LiquidCrystal library to show text on an LCD with no I2C backpack.

scripts.title: LCD Custom Characters (Hearts and Smileys)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LiquidCrystal I2C"; LCD SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Draws your own little pictures (a heart, a smiley and a walking person) on an LCD.

scripts.title: LCD Dino Jump Game
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LiquidCrystal I2C"; LCD SDA A4, SCL A5, VCC 5V, GND; jump button between pin 2 and GND.
scripts.about: An endless runner on a 16x2 LCD: press the button to make the dino jump over cactuses.

scripts.title: LCD Score Counter with Buttons
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LiquidCrystal I2C"; LCD SDA A4, SCL A5; plus button pin 2 to GND, minus button pin 3 to GND, reset button pin 4 to GND.
scripts.about: A score counter: one button adds a point, one takes a point away, and one resets to zero.

scripts.title: LCD Scrolling Message
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LiquidCrystal I2C"; LCD SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Scrolls a long message across the top line of a 16x2 LCD like a news ticker.

scripts.title: LCD Stopwatch with Lap Times
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LiquidCrystal I2C"; LCD SDA A4, SCL A5; start/stop button pin 2 to GND; lap/reset button pin 3 to GND.
scripts.about: A stopwatch showing minutes, seconds and hundredths, with a lap time on the second line.

scripts.title: LED Blinker Class (Many LEDs, No delay)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LEDs with 220 ohm resistors on pins 3, 4, 5 and 6.
scripts.about: Makes a small Blinker class so each LED keeps its own on and off times, then runs four of them together.

scripts.title: LED Dice with Seven LEDs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 7 LEDs (220 ohm) arranged like dice dots: top-left 2, top-right 3, middle-left 4, center 5, middle-right 6, bottom-left 7, bottom-right 8; button pin 10 to GND.
scripts.about: Shows a dice roll as real dice dots using seven LEDs when you press the button.

scripts.title: LED Dimmer Knob
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; potentiometer middle leg to A0 (outer legs 5V and GND); LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 9.
scripts.about: Turning a knob makes an LED dimmer or brighter.

scripts.title: LED that Gets Brighter in the Dark
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; photoresistor from 5V to A0 with a 10k resistor from A0 to GND; LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 9 (a PWM pin).
scripts.about: Smoothly makes an LED brighter as the room gets darker, using PWM.

scripts.title: Light Meter Bar in Serial Monitor
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; photoresistor from 5V to A0, and a 10k resistor from A0 to GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Reads a light sensor and draws a bar of # signs that grows when it gets brighter.

scripts.title: Light Seeking Robot
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot car; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6; left photoresistor 5V to A0 (10k from A0 to GND), right one the same on A1; point them forward-left and forward-right.
scripts.about: Steers toward the brightest light, so it chases a flashlight around the room.

scripts.title: Light Theremin
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; photoresistor from 5V to A0 with a 10k resistor from A0 to GND; passive buzzer on pin 8. Wave your hand over the sensor.
scripts.about: Plays higher or lower notes as you move your hand over a light sensor, after learning the room's light.

scripts.title: Line Follower Robot (2 Sensors)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot car; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6; left IR line sensor OUT to A0, right to A1 (both on the front, either side of the black line).
scripts.about: Follows a black tape line on the floor using two IR sensors and two motors.

scripts.title: Magic 8 Ball on an LCD
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LiquidCrystal I2C"; LCD SDA A4, SCL A5; tilt switch between pin 2 and GND (or a button). Ask a question and shake it!
scripts.about: Shake the tilt switch and the LCD shows a random Magic 8 Ball answer.

scripts.title: Magnet Detector (Hall Sensor)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; KY-003 or A3144 hall sensor signal to pin 2 (with 10k pull-up or INPUT_PULLUP), VCC 5V, GND; LED on pin 13.
scripts.about: Lights an LED and prints a message when a magnet comes near the hall effect sensor.

scripts.title: Math Quiz in the Serial Monitor
scripts.where: Any Arduino; open Serial Monitor at 9600 with line ending "Newline"; type answers and press Enter. Optional buzzer on pin 8.
scripts.about: Asks 10 random add, subtract and multiply questions, beeps for right or wrong, and gives a final score.

scripts.title: Mini Sumo Robot
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6; HC-SR04 forward Trig A2, Echo A3; IR line sensor pointing down at the front, OUT to A0 (sees the white ring edge); start button pin 2 to GND.
scripts.about: Waits 5 seconds after the start button, then hunts for the enemy robot, charges it, and avoids the white ring edge.

scripts.title: Mini Weather Station
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "DHT sensor library" and "LiquidCrystal I2C"; DHT11 data pin 2; photoresistor 5V to A0 with 10k to GND; LCD SDA A4, SCL A5; button pin 3 to GND switches pages.
scripts.about: Shows temperature, humidity, light level and today's lowest and highest temperature on LCD pages you flip with a button.

scripts.title: Mood Lamp with a Mode Button
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; RGB LED red 9, green 10, blue 11 (220 ohm each); push button between pin 2 and GND.
scripts.about: Each button press changes the lamp mode: warm, cool, party flash, slow rainbow or off.

scripts.title: Morse Code Translator
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LED on pin 13 (built in) and passive buzzer on pin 8; open Serial Monitor at 9600, type a message and press Enter.
scripts.about: Turns any message you type into Morse code beeps and flashes, and prints the dots and dashes.

scripts.title: Motion Light that Stays On
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; PIR OUT to pin 2; LED (220 ohm) or relay IN on pin 9.
scripts.about: Turns a light on when motion is seen and keeps it on until nobody has moved for 20 seconds.

scripts.title: Motion Visitor Counter
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; PIR OUT to pin 2, VCC 5V, GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600. Set the PIR jumper to single trigger (L).
scripts.about: Counts how many times the PIR sensor starts seeing motion and prints the total.

scripts.title: MPU6050 Tilt Angles (No Library)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; MPU6050 VCC to 5V, GND to GND, SDA to A4, SCL to A5; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Talks to an MPU6050 over I2C and works out how much it is tilted forward and sideways.

scripts.title: MQ-2 Gas and Smoke Sensor
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; MQ-2 module AO to A0, VCC 5V, GND; buzzer pin 8; open Serial Monitor at 9600. It gets warm, and needs a few minutes to heat up.
scripts.about: Warms up the MQ-2 sensor, learns the clean air level, then warns when smoke or gas makes it rise.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Campfire Flicker
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; strip or ring DIN to pin 6 (330 ohm), 5V, GND; put it behind paper for a cosy fake fire.
scripts.about: Flickers a NeoPixel strip in reds, oranges and yellows like a real fire.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Color Picker Button
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; strip DIN to pin 6, 5V, GND; push button between pin 2 and GND.
scripts.about: Each button press changes the whole strip to the next color in a list.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Color Wipe
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; strip DIN to pin 6 through a 330 ohm resistor, 5V and GND (use an external 5V supply for more than 30 LEDs).
scripts.about: Fills a NeoPixel strip one LED at a time with red, then green, then blue.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Knob Level Meter
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; strip DIN to pin 6, 5V, GND; potentiometer middle leg on A0 (or any analog sensor).
scripts.about: Shows a knob's position as a bar on an LED strip that goes green, then yellow, then red.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Police Lights
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; 8 or more LEDs, DIN to pin 6, 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Flashes the left half red and the right half blue like a police car.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Rainbow
scripts.where: Install "Adafruit NeoPixel" from the Arduino IDE Library Manager, paste this into a new sketch and upload it; wire the strip's DIN to pin 6, 5V to 5V and GND to GND.
scripts.about: Makes a NeoPixel LED strip show a smooth rainbow that slides along.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Ring Loading Spinner
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; 12 or 16 LED ring, DIN to pin 6, 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Spins a glowing comet with a fading tail around a NeoPixel ring, changing color as it goes.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Theater Chase Lights
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; strip DIN to pin 6 (330 ohm resistor), 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Makes lights march along a strip like an old cinema sign, changing color each round.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Tug of War Button Battle
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; 30 LED strip DIN to pin 6, 5V, GND; red player button pin 2 to GND, blue player button pin 3 to GND.
scripts.about: Two players mash their buttons to pull the light to their end of the strip; first to reach the end wins.

scripts.title: NeoPixel Twinkling Stars
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; strip DIN to pin 6, 5V, GND; great on a bedroom ceiling.
scripts.about: Makes random LEDs sparkle white and slowly fade, like stars twinkling.

scripts.title: Night Light with a Light Sensor
scripts.where: Paste this into a new Arduino IDE sketch and upload it; wire a photoresistor from 5V to A0, a 10k resistor from A0 to GND, and an LED (long leg) through a 220 ohm resistor to pin 9 with the short leg to GND.
scripts.about: Makes an LED glow brighter as the room gets darker, like a night light.

scripts.title: NTC Thermistor Thermometer
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 10k NTC thermistor from 5V to A0, and a 10k resistor from A0 to GND (or use a KY-013 module); open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Works out the temperature from a thermistor using the beta equation.

scripts.title: Obstacle Avoiding Robot
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot car; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6; HC-SR04 on the front, Trig A2, Echo A3.
scripts.about: Drives forward and, when a wall gets close, backs up and turns a random way before carrying on.

scripts.title: OLED Bouncing Ball
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit SSD1306" and "Adafruit GFX Library"; OLED SDA A4, SCL A5, VCC 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Bounces a ball around the OLED screen with a little gravity, so it slowly settles down.

scripts.title: OLED Flappy Bird
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit SSD1306" and "Adafruit GFX Library"; OLED SDA A4, SCL A5, VCC 5V, GND; flap button between pin 2 and GND.
scripts.about: Tap the button to flap and fly a little bird through gaps in the pipes.

scripts.title: OLED Live Sensor Graph
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit SSD1306" and "Adafruit GFX Library"; OLED SDA A4, SCL A5; any analog sensor or knob on A0.
scripts.about: Draws a scrolling line graph of a sensor on the OLED, with the current number at the top.

scripts.title: OLED Pong for Two Players
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit SSD1306" and "Adafruit GFX Library"; OLED SDA A4, SCL A5; left paddle knob middle leg on A0, right paddle knob on A1; buzzer pin 8.
scripts.about: Classic Pong on an OLED where each player turns a knob to move their paddle; first to 5 wins.

scripts.title: OLED Robot Eyes
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit SSD1306" and "Adafruit GFX Library"; OLED SDA A4, SCL A5, VCC 5V, GND; stick it on your robot's face.
scripts.about: Draws two robot eyes that look around, blink and sometimes look happy.

scripts.title: OLED Shapes Drawing
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit SSD1306" and "Adafruit GFX Library"; OLED SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Draws lines, rectangles, circles and triangles on an OLED, one shape show after another.

scripts.title: OLED SSD1306 Hello World
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit SSD1306" and "Adafruit GFX Library"; 128x64 I2C OLED VCC to 5V, GND, SDA to A4, SCL to A5.
scripts.about: Shows big and small text on a little 0.96 inch OLED screen.

scripts.title: Pan and Tilt with a Joystick
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; joystick VRx to A0, VRy to A1, SW to pin 2, 5V, GND; pan servo on pin 9, tilt servo on pin 10; power servos from a 5V supply with GND shared.
scripts.about: Moves two servos smoothly with a joystick, and the joystick button re-centers them.

scripts.title: Parking Sensor with Beeps
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; HC-SR04 Trig to pin 9, Echo to pin 10, VCC to 5V, GND to GND; piezo buzzer + to pin 8, - to GND.
scripts.about: Beeps slowly when something is far away and faster and faster as it gets closer, like a car.

scripts.title: PIR Motion Alarm
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; HC-SR501 PIR OUT to pin 2, VCC to 5V, GND to GND; red LED (220 ohm) on pin 13; buzzer + on pin 8.
scripts.about: Flashes a light and sounds a siren when the PIR sensor sees someone move.

scripts.title: Plant Soil Moisture Monitor
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; soil moisture sensor AO to A0, VCC to pin 7 (so it is only powered while reading), GND; green LED pin 4, red LED pin 5 (220 ohm each).
scripts.about: Checks how wet the soil is and lights green when the plant is happy or red when it needs water.

scripts.title: Police Siren Sound
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; passive piezo buzzer + to pin 8, - to GND (an active buzzer only beeps one note).
scripts.about: Makes a wailing siren and a fast yelp siren with a passive buzzer.

scripts.title: Pomodoro Study Timer
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; red LED (220 ohm) on pin 9 for focus time, green LED on pin 10 for break time; buzzer pin 8; button pin 2 to GND to start; Serial Monitor 9600 shows minutes left.
scripts.about: Times 25 minutes of focus (red light) then a 5 minute break (green light), and repeats, beeping at each change.

scripts.title: Reaction Game that Saves the High Score
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LED on pin 9; button pin 2 to GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600. Hold the button while pressing reset to clear the record.
scripts.about: A reaction game whose best time is stored in EEPROM, so the record stays even when the Arduino is turned off.

scripts.title: Reaction Time Tester
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 9; push button between pin 2 and GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Waits a random time, turns on an LED, and measures how many milliseconds you take to press the button.

scripts.title: Read a 4x4 Keypad
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Keypad" by Mark Stanley; keypad pins 1 to 8 (left to right) go to Arduino pins 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Prints each key you press on a 4x4 membrane keypad.

scripts.title: Read a Joystick
scripts.where: Paste this into a new Arduino IDE sketch, upload it and open Tools > Serial Monitor at 9600 baud; wire the joystick VRx to A0, VRy to A1, SW to pin 2, +5V to 5V and GND to GND.
scripts.about: Reads a joystick's X and Y and its press button, then prints them and which way it is pushed.

scripts.title: Read a Potentiometer and its Voltage
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; potentiometer outer legs to 5V and GND, middle leg to A0; open Serial Monitor at 9600 (or Tools > Serial Plotter).
scripts.about: Reads a knob, then prints the raw number, the voltage and a percentage.

scripts.title: Relay Lamp On and Off Timer
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 5V relay module IN to pin 7, VCC 5V, GND GND; switch a LOW voltage device only (like a 12V LED strip), never mains without an adult.
scripts.about: Clicks a relay on for 5 seconds and off for 5 seconds to switch a lamp or LED strip.

scripts.title: Relay Toggle Button
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; relay module IN to pin 7, VCC 5V, GND; push button between pin 2 and GND; LED on pin 13 shows the state.
scripts.about: Each button press flips a relay on or off, like a normal light switch.

scripts.title: RFID Card Reader (RC522)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "MFRC522"; RC522 SDA to 10, SCK to 13, MOSI to 11, MISO to 12, RST to 9, 3.3V to 3.3V (not 5V!), GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Prints the ID number of any RFID card or key tag you hold near the reader.

scripts.title: RFID Door Lock with a Servo
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; RC522 wired as SDA 10, SCK 13, MOSI 11, MISO 12, RST 9, 3.3V, GND; servo on pin 6; green LED pin 4, red LED pin 5. Put your card's ID (from the reader sketch) in MY_CARD.
scripts.about: Unlocks a servo latch for 3 seconds when the right RFID card is scanned and flashes red for wrong ones.

scripts.title: RGB LED Color Mixer
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; common cathode RGB LED: longest leg to GND, red leg to pin 9, green to 10, blue to 11, each through a 220 ohm resistor.
scripts.about: Shows red, green, blue, yellow, purple, cyan, orange and white on one RGB LED.

scripts.title: RGB LED Rainbow Fade
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; common cathode RGB LED: red to pin 9, green to 10, blue to 11 (220 ohm each), long leg to GND.
scripts.about: Smoothly fades one RGB LED through every color of the rainbow.

scripts.title: RGB LED with Three Knobs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; three potentiometers with middle legs on A0 (red), A1 (green), A2 (blue); RGB LED red to 9, green to 10, blue to 11 with 220 ohm resistors; Serial Monitor 9600.
scripts.about: Lets you mix any color on an RGB LED with three knobs and prints the color code.

scripts.title: Robot Arm Record and Play Back
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; servos base 3, shoulder 5, elbow 6, claw 9 (own 5V supply, GND joined); potentiometers A0 to A3; record button pin 2 to GND; play button pin 4 to GND.
scripts.about: Press record to save the arm's position (up to 20 poses), then press play to make it repeat them all.

scripts.title: Robot Arm with Four Knobs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 4 servos (base pin 3, shoulder 5, elbow 6, claw 9) powered by a separate 5V 2A supply with GND joined; 4 potentiometers on A0 to A3.
scripts.about: Controls a 4-servo robot arm (base, shoulder, elbow and claw) with four knobs, moving smoothly.

scripts.title: Robot Motor Speed Matcher
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot car; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6; open Serial Monitor at 9600 with "Newline"; type l or r to trim, g to go.
scripts.about: Helps your robot drive straight by letting you trim the left or right motor speed from the Serial Monitor.

scripts.title: Robot that Won't Fall Off the Table
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot car; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6; two IR obstacle sensors pointing DOWN at the front corners, left OUT to A0, right OUT to A1.
scripts.about: Drives around a table and backs away whenever a downward IR sensor sees the edge.

scripts.title: Rock Paper Scissors vs Arduino
scripts.where: Any Arduino; open Serial Monitor at 9600; type r, p or s and press Enter. Optional: green LED on pin 4 (you win), red LED on pin 5 (Arduino wins).
scripts.about: Play rock paper scissors against the Arduino by typing r, p or s, and it keeps score.

scripts.title: Rotary Encoder Counter
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; KY-040 rotary encoder CLK to pin 2, DT to pin 3, SW to pin 4, + to 5V, GND to GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Counts up and down as you turn a rotary encoder, and resets to zero when you push it.

scripts.title: RPM Meter with a Hall Sensor
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; A3144 hall sensor signal to pin 2 (INPUT_PULLUP), VCC 5V, GND; glue one small magnet on the spinning wheel or fan; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Counts how many times a magnet passes the sensor each second and shows the speed in RPM.

scripts.title: Save Settings with a Struct in EEPROM
scripts.where: Any Arduino Uno or Nano; open Serial Monitor at 9600 with "Newline"; type commands like volume 7, name Bolt, show, reset.
scripts.about: Keeps a group of settings (volume, brightness and a robot name) in one struct and saves them all to EEPROM at once.

scripts.title: Secret Knock Detector
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; piezo disc + to A0 and - to GND, with a 1 megohm resistor across A0 and GND; LED on pin 13; tape the piezo to a door or box.
scripts.about: Listens for knocks with a piezo disc and lights up after three knocks in a row.

scripts.title: Sensor Data Logger (CSV)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; light sensor on A0 (photoresistor + 10k), temperature TMP36 on A1; open Serial Monitor at 9600, then copy the lines into a spreadsheet.
scripts.about: Prints the time, light level and temperature every 5 seconds as CSV lines that paste straight into a spreadsheet.

scripts.title: Serial Plotter Wave Drawing
scripts.where: Any Arduino; upload, then open Tools > Serial Plotter at 9600 (not the Serial Monitor).
scripts.about: Draws a sine wave, a square wave and a sawtooth wave as three colored lines in the Serial Plotter.

scripts.title: Servo Door with a Button
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; servo signal to pin 9, red 5V, brown GND; push button between pin 2 and GND.
scripts.about: Opens and closes a little door with a servo each time you press the button, moving slowly so it looks smooth.

scripts.title: Servo Follows a Knob
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; potentiometer middle leg to A0; servo signal (orange) to pin 9, red 5V, brown GND.
scripts.about: Makes a servo point wherever you turn the knob.

scripts.title: Servo Sweep
scripts.where: Paste this into a new Arduino IDE sketch and upload it; wire the servo's signal (orange or yellow) to pin 9, red to 5V, and brown or black to GND.
scripts.about: Swings a servo motor slowly from 0 to 180 degrees and back, over and over.

scripts.title: Short Press vs Long Press
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; push button between pin 2 and GND; LED on pin 9 (220 ohm); open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Tells a quick tap from a long hold: a tap changes the LED brightness and a 1 second hold turns it off.

scripts.title: Simon Says Memory Game
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 4 LEDs (220 ohm) on pins 8, 9, 10, 11; 4 buttons from pins 2, 3, 4, 5 to GND (button 2 matches LED 8 and so on); passive buzzer on pin 12.
scripts.about: Plays a growing pattern of lights and sounds that you must copy with the buttons, one step longer each round.

scripts.title: Simple Clock on a TM1637 Display
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "TM1637" by Avishay Orpaz; display CLK to 2, DIO to 3, VCC 5V, GND; hour button pin 4 to GND, minute button pin 5 to GND.
scripts.about: A 24-hour clock with a blinking colon that you set with an hour button and a minute button.

scripts.title: Single 7-Segment Display Counter
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; common cathode 7-segment display: segments a to g on pins 2 to 8 (each through a 220 ohm resistor), dot on pin 9, common pins to GND.
scripts.about: Counts from 0 to 9 on a single 7-segment display by lighting the right segments.

scripts.title: Single Click vs Double Click
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; push button between pin 2 and GND; green LED pin 4, blue LED pin 5 (220 ohm each); open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Detects whether you clicked once or twice quickly and toggles a different LED for each.

scripts.title: Smart Robot that Looks Both Ways
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot car; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 2, IN4 4, ENB 6; HC-SR04 Trig A2, Echo A3, sitting on a servo on pin 3. (Pins 9 and 10 lose PWM when the Servo library runs.)
scripts.about: When it finds a wall, the robot turns its head left and right, then drives toward whichever side is more open.

scripts.title: Smooth Line Follower (3 Sensors, P Control)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot car; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6; three IR line sensors left A0, middle A1, right A2.
scripts.about: Follows a line smoothly by working out how far off-center it is and steering in proportion.

scripts.title: Smooth Out Jumpy Sensor Readings
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; any analog sensor or potentiometer on A0; open Tools > Serial Plotter at 9600 to see both lines.
scripts.about: Keeps the last 10 readings and averages them, then plots the raw and smooth values together.

scripts.title: Smooth Servo Without delay()
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; servo signal on pin 9; LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 13 (or just the built-in LED).
keywords: servo and blink at the same time
scripts.about: Sweeps a servo smoothly using millis() so an LED can blink at its own speed at the same time.

scripts.title: Snake Game on an 8x8 LED Matrix
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LedControl"; MAX7219 matrix DIN 12, CLK 11, CS 10, VCC 5V, GND; joystick VRx A0, VRy A1, 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Plays Snake on an 8x8 LED matrix: steer with a joystick, eat the blinking food and don't bite yourself.

scripts.title: SOS Signal Light
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; uses the built-in LED on pin 13, or add a bright LED with a 220 ohm resistor on pin 13.
scripts.about: Flashes S O S in Morse code: three short, three long, three short.

scripts.title: Sound Level Meter with LEDs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; sound sensor AO to A0, VCC 5V, GND; 5 LEDs with 220 ohm resistors on pins 3 to 7 (green, green, yellow, yellow, red).
scripts.about: Listens with a microphone module and lights more LEDs the louder it is.

scripts.title: Steer a Servo with a Remote
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "IRremote" (version 4+); IR receiver OUT to pin 11; servo signal to pin 9, red 5V, brown GND. Codes are for the common Car MP3 remote.
scripts.about: Moves a servo left or right a bit each time you press the arrow buttons on a remote.

scripts.title: Stepper Follows a Knob
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 28BYJ-48 with ULN2003: IN1 8, IN2 9, IN3 10, IN4 11; potentiometer middle leg on A0.
scripts.about: Makes a stepper motor's pointer copy the position of a knob, like a remote dial.

scripts.title: Stepper Left and Right Buttons
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 28BYJ-48 with ULN2003 IN1 8, IN2 9, IN3 10, IN4 11; left button pin 2 to GND, right button pin 3 to GND.
scripts.about: Turns the stepper one way while you hold the left button and the other way with the right button.

scripts.title: Stepper Motor 28BYJ-48
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 28BYJ-48 stepper on a ULN2003 board: IN1 to 8, IN2 to 9, IN3 to 10, IN4 to 11, + to 5V, - to GND.
scripts.about: Turns a small stepper motor exactly one full turn one way, then one full turn back.

scripts.title: Stop the Light Arcade Game
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 7 LEDs (220 ohm) on pins 3 to 9, the middle one (pin 6) a different color; button pin 2 to GND; buzzer pin 11.
scripts.about: A light races along the LEDs and you must press the button exactly when it reaches the middle one.

scripts.title: Thermostat Fan with DHT11 and a Relay
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; DHT11 data to pin 2; relay module IN to pin 7, VCC to 5V, GND to GND; the fan goes through the relay with its own power supply.
scripts.about: Turns a fan on through a relay when it gets too hot and off again when it cools down.

scripts.title: Tilt Switch Alarm
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; tilt (ball) switch between pin 2 and GND; LED (220 ohm) on pin 13; buzzer on pin 8.
scripts.about: Beeps and flashes when the tilt switch is tipped over, like an anti-theft box.

scripts.title: TM1637 4-Digit Display Counter
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "TM1637" by Avishay Orpaz; display CLK to pin 2, DIO to pin 3, VCC 5V, GND; button between pin 4 and GND.
scripts.about: Shows a number on a 4-digit display that goes up each time you press the button.

scripts.title: TMP36 Temperature Sensor
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; TMP36 flat side facing you: left leg 5V, middle leg A0, right leg GND; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Turns the TMP36 sensor's voltage into degrees Celsius and Fahrenheit.

scripts.title: Touch Sensor Lamp
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; TTP223 touch module SIG to pin 2, VCC 5V, GND; LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 9.
scripts.about: Each tap on the touch pad changes a lamp between off, dim, medium and bright.

scripts.title: Touchless Smart Trash Can
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; HC-SR04 on the front of the can, Trig 9, Echo 10; servo on pin 6 tied to the lid with string or a stick; power the servo from 5V.
scripts.about: Opens the trash can lid with a servo when your hand comes close and closes it a few seconds later.

scripts.title: Traffic Light
scripts.where: Paste this into a new Arduino IDE sketch and upload it; wire a red LED to pin 12, yellow to pin 11 and green to pin 10, each through a 220 ohm resistor, with every short leg going to GND.
scripts.about: Runs three LEDs like a real traffic light: green, yellow, then red.

scripts.title: Traffic Light State Machine with Crossing Button
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; car lights red 4, yellow 5, green 6; walker lights red 7, green 8 (220 ohm each); crossing button pin 2 to GND; buzzer pin 9.
scripts.about: A pedestrian crossing built as a state machine with millis(), so the button is noticed at any moment.

scripts.title: TV Remote Controlled Robot Car
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "IRremote" (version 4+); IR receiver OUT to pin 12; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6. Codes are for the Car MP3 remote; use the code finder sketch for yours.
scripts.about: Drives a robot car with an infrared remote: 2 forward, 8 back, 4 left, 6 right, 5 stop.

scripts.title: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star with LEDs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; passive buzzer on pin 8; optional LEDs with 220 ohm resistors on pins 2 to 7, one for each note.
scripts.about: Plays Twinkle Twinkle Little Star and lights a different LED for each note, like a music box.

scripts.title: Two Arduinos Talking: Receiver (I2C Slave)
scripts.where: Upload to Arduino #2; join A4 to A4, A5 to A5 and GND to GND with Arduino #1 (running the Sender sketch); LED with 220 ohm resistor on pin 9.
scripts.about: Listens on I2C address 8 and sets an LED's brightness to whatever number the sender Arduino sends.

scripts.title: Two Arduinos Talking: Sender (I2C Master)
scripts.where: Upload to Arduino #1; join A4 to A4, A5 to A5 and GND to GND between two Unos; potentiometer middle leg on A0. Load the Receiver sketch on Arduino #2.
scripts.about: Reads a knob and sends its value to a second Arduino over I2C ten times a second.

scripts.title: Two Minute Toothbrush Timer
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "Adafruit NeoPixel"; 8 LED stick or ring DIN to pin 6, 5V, GND; button pin 2 to GND; passive buzzer pin 8.
scripts.about: Fills an LED bar over two minutes, beeping every 30 seconds so you know when to brush the next part of your mouth.

scripts.title: Two Player Quick Draw Duel
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; player 1 button pin 2 to GND with LED on pin 8; player 2 button pin 3 to GND with LED on pin 9; middle "go" LED on pin 10; buzzer on pin 11.
scripts.about: Two players wait for the go light; the first to press wins, but pressing too early loses.

scripts.title: Two Servos Waving Arms
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; left arm servo on pin 9, right arm servo on pin 10; power servos from 5V (or a 4xAA pack with GND joined to Arduino GND).
scripts.about: Makes two servo arms wave hello, flap together and then do a mirror wave.

scripts.title: Type an Angle to Move a Servo
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; servo signal on pin 9; open Serial Monitor at 9600, set line ending to Newline, type a number 0 to 180 and press Enter.
scripts.about: Moves a servo to whatever angle you type into the Serial Monitor.

scripts.title: Type Commands to Control LEDs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; red LED pin 9, green LED pin 10, blue LED pin 11 (220 ohm each); open Serial Monitor at 9600 with line ending "Newline".
scripts.about: Understands typed commands like "red on", "all off" and "blink green" to control three LEDs.

scripts.title: Ultrasonic Distance Sensor
scripts.where: Paste this into a new Arduino IDE sketch, upload it and open Tools > Serial Monitor at 9600 baud; wire the HC-SR04 VCC to 5V, GND to GND, Trig to pin 9 and Echo to pin 10.
scripts.about: Measures how far away something is with an HC-SR04 sensor and prints it in centimeters.

scripts.title: Ultrasonic Radar Sweep
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; servo signal to pin 11 (red 5V, brown GND); HC-SR04 glued on the servo horn, Trig to 9, Echo to 10; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Sweeps an ultrasonic sensor back and forth on a servo and prints the angle and distance like a radar.

scripts.title: Ultrasonic Ruler on an LCD
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; install "LiquidCrystal I2C"; HC-SR04 Trig to 9, Echo to 10; LCD I2C SDA to A4, SCL to A5, VCC 5V, GND.
scripts.about: Measures distance with an HC-SR04 and shows it in cm and inches on an LCD.

scripts.title: Wall Following Robot
scripts.where: Arduino Uno robot car; L298N ENA 5, IN1 7, IN2 8, IN3 9, IN4 10, ENB 6; HC-SR04 pointing to the RIGHT side, Trig A2, Echo A3; another HC-SR04 pointing forward, Trig A4, Echo A5.
scripts.about: Drives along a wall on its right, keeping about 15 cm away, and turns left at corners.

scripts.title: Water Flow Meter (YF-S201)
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; YF-S201 flow sensor red to 5V, black to GND, yellow to pin 2; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Counts pulses from a water flow sensor to show liters per minute and the total liters used.

scripts.title: Water Level Sensor
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; water level sensor S to A0, + to pin 7, - to GND; buzzer on pin 8; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: Measures how deep the water is on the sensor and beeps when it gets too high.

scripts.title: Whack-a-Mole with LEDs
scripts.where: Arduino Uno; 4 LEDs (220 ohm) on pins 8 to 11; 4 buttons from pins 2 to 5 to GND (in the same order); buzzer on pin 12; open Serial Monitor at 9600.
scripts.about: A random LED lights up and you must hit its button before it goes out; the game gets faster as you score.

scripts.title: 2D Arrays: a Game Map Grid
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o grid && ./grid
scripts.about: Stores a little game map in a 2D array of characters, prints it, counts the coins, and moves a player around.

scripts.title: Abstract Classes and Interfaces
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o devices && ./devices
scripts.about: Defines a Device interface with pure virtual functions, then makes a lamp, a fan and a robot that all follow it.

scripts.title: Arrays: Lists of Numbers
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o arrays && ./arrays
scripts.about: Stores a week of temperatures in an array, then finds the total, average, hottest and coldest day.

scripts.title: Asking the User for Input
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o input && ./input
scripts.about: Asks for your full name, age and favorite number, checks the answers are valid, and talks back.

scripts.title: auto and Range-Based for Loops
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o autoloop && ./autoloop
scripts.about: Shows how auto guesses types for you and how range-based for loops walk through vectors and maps.

scripts.title: Bank Account Class (Encapsulation)
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o bank && ./bank
scripts.about: A BankAccount class keeps its balance private so it can only change through safe deposit and withdraw methods.

scripts.title: Bitwise Operators and Flags
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o bits && ./bits
scripts.about: Uses single bits as on and off switches for a player's power-ups, with &, |, ^, ~ and shifts.

scripts.title: Callbacks with std::function
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o events && ./events
scripts.about: Builds a tiny event system where functions are stored in a list and called when something happens, like in game engines.

scripts.title: Checking Characters (Password Strength)
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o strength && ./strength
scripts.about: Uses isupper, islower, isdigit and ispunct to rate how strong a typed password is.

scripts.title: Class Template: an Inventory Bag
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o bag && ./bag
scripts.about: Builds a Bag class template with a fixed number of slots that can hold any type of item.

scripts.title: Classes and Objects: a Pet
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o pets && ./pets
scripts.about: Makes a Pet class with a name, hunger and happiness, then creates two pets and plays with them.

scripts.title: Command Line Arguments (argc and argv)
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp, compile with g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o greet, then run ./greet Storm --shout --times 3
scripts.about: Reads words typed after the program name, like a name and flags such as --shout and --times 3.

scripts.title: const and constexpr: Values that Never Change
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o constexpr && ./constexpr
scripts.about: Shows const variables, constexpr functions worked out while compiling, static_assert checks, and const methods.

scripts.title: Constructors and Destructors
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o lifecycle && ./lifecycle
scripts.about: Shows when objects are born and when they are destroyed, using a torch that lights up and goes out.

scripts.title: Copy vs Move (std::move)
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o move && ./move
scripts.about: Shows the difference between copying a big object and moving it, with a class that prints when each happens.

scripts.title: Countdown Timer
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o timer && ./timer
scripts.about: Asks how many seconds to count down, ticks once a second, then shows how long it really took.

scripts.title: Diary that Saves to a File
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o diary && ./diary (it creates diary.txt next to it)
scripts.about: A little diary that adds your new entry to the end of diary.txt and then shows all the entries so far.

scripts.title: Enums: Naming Your Options
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o enums && ./enums
scripts.about: Uses enum class to name directions and weather types, then switches on them to make choices.

scripts.title: Exceptions: try, throw and catch
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o exceptions && ./exceptions
scripts.about: Shows how to throw an error when something goes wrong and catch it so the program doesn't crash.

scripts.title: Function Overloading and Default Arguments
scripts.where: Save as main.cpp and run: g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o overload && ./overload
scripts.about: Shows how several functions can share one name with different inputs, and how default arguments fill in missing values.

scripts.title: Classes: Virtual Pet
scripts.where: Save as pet.py and run: python3 pet.py
scripts.about: Builds a Pet class with hunger and happiness, then makes two pets and plays with them.
scripts.code:
class Pet:
    """A blueprint for pets. Each pet made from it is an object."""

    def __init__(self, name, species):
        # __init__ runs when a new pet is made. self means "this pet".
        self.name = name
        self.species = species
        self.hunger = 50
        self.happiness = 50

    def feed(self):
        self.hunger = max(0, self.hunger - 30)
        print(f"{self.name} munches some food. Yum!")

    def play(self):
        self.happiness = min(100, self.happiness + 25)
        self.hunger = min(100, self.hunger + 10)
        print(f"{self.name} plays fetch and looks so happy!")

    def mood(self):
        if self.hunger > 70:
            return "hungry"
        if self.happiness > 70:
            return "super happy"
        return "okay"

    def __str__(self):
        # __str__ decides what print(pet) shows.
        return f"{self.name} the {self.species}: hunger {self.hunger}, happiness {self.happiness}, feels {self.mood()}"


rex = Pet("Rex", "dog")
whiskers = Pet("Whiskers", "cat")

rex.play()
rex.play()
whiskers.feed()

print(rex)
print(whiskers)

# *args collects any number of extra values into a tuple

print("add_all(1, 2, 3, 4, 5) =", add_all(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))


# **kwargs collects extra named values into a dictionary

    for stat, value in stats.items():
        print(f"  {stat} = {value}")


build_character("Knight", strength=9, speed=4, magic=1)


# You can also "unpack" a list or dict into a function call

scripts.title: Doing Two Things at Once
scripts.where: Save as threads.py and run: python3 threads.py
keywords: python run at the same time
scripts.about: Uses threads so two pretend downloads run at the same time instead of one after another.
scripts.code:
import threading
import time


def download(name, seconds):
    print(f"Starting {name}...")
    for step in range(1, 4):
        time.sleep(seconds / 3)
        print(f"  {name} is {step * 33}% done")
    print(f"Finished {name}!")


start = time.perf_counter()

# Make two threads. Each one runs its own function.
a = threading.Thread(target=download, args=("music.mp3", 1.5))
b = threading.Thread(target=download, args=("game.zip", 1.5))
a.start()
b.start()

# join() waits until each thread is done
a.join()
b.join()

print(f"Both done in {time.perf_counter() - start:.1f} seconds (not 3, because they overlapped!)")

fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]

# enumerate gives you the position AND the item
for index, fruit in enumerate(fruits):
    print(index, fruit)

# start=1 makes a nicer numbered list

    print(f"{number}. {fruit}")

# zip pairs up items from two (or more) lists
names = ["Storm", "Doodle", "Nova"]
scores = [88, 95, 72]
for name, score in zip(names, scores):
    print(f"{name} scored {score}")

# zip can build a dictionary
score_book = dict(zip(names, scores))
print("Score book:", score_book)

# zip three lists at once
emojis = ["lightning", "pencil", "star"]
for name, score, emoji in zip(names, scores, emojis):
    print(f"{name:<8}{score:>4}  ({emoji})")

# Both together: find which position has the top score
best_index = 0
for i, score in enumerate(scores):
    if score > scores[best_index]:
        best_index = i
print("Winner:", names[best_index])

scripts.code:
import time
from enum import Enum


class Light(Enum):
    GREEN = "go"
    YELLOW = "slow down"
    RED = "stop"


# Which light comes next, and how long each one lasts (seconds)
NEXT = {Light.GREEN: Light.YELLOW, Light.YELLOW: Light.RED, Light.RED: Light.GREEN}
TIME = {Light.GREEN: 1.5, Light.YELLOW: 0.5, Light.RED: 1.5}

light = Light.RED
for _ in range(6):
    print(f"{light.name:<6} means {light.value}")
    time.sleep(TIME[light])
    light = NEXT[light]

# Enums can be listed and compared safely
print("All lights:", [l.name for l in Light])
print("Is it red?", light == Light.RED)
print("Look up by value:", Light("stop"))

# break stops the loop early, continue skips to the next round
for n in range(1, 20):

    if n > 10:

scripts.about: Shows how to make your own functions with def, pass them values and get answers back with return.
scripts.code:
# A function is a reusable chunk of code with a name.
def say_hi():
    print("Hi there!")


# Parameters are the inputs a function needs.
def greet(name):
    print(f"Hello, {name}!")


# return sends an answer back to whoever called the function.
def add(a, b):
    return a + b


def area_of_rectangle(width, height):
    return width * height


# A function can return True or False to answer a yes or no question.
def is_even(number):
    return number % 2 == 0


# A function can use other functions!
def describe(number):
    kind = "even" if is_even(number) else "odd"
    return f"{number} is {kind}"


say_hi()
greet("Storm")
greet("Doodle")
print("3 + 4 =", add(3, 4))
print("A 5 by 8 rectangle has area", area_of_rectangle(5, 8))
for n in range(1, 6):
    print(describe(n))

scripts.about: Shows how yield makes functions that hand out values one at a time, even forever.
scripts.code:
def count_up_to(limit):
    n = 1
    while n <= limit:
        yield n       # hand back one value, then pause here until asked for the next
        n += 1


def fibonacci():
    a, b = 0, 1

import random


def merge(left, right):
    """Join two sorted lists into one sorted list."""
    result = []
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
        if left[i] <= right[j]:
            result.append(left[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            result.append(right[j])
            j += 1
    result.extend(left[i:])   # whatever is left over is already sorted
    result.extend(right[j:])
    return result


def merge_sort(items):
    if len(items) <= 1:  # a list of 0 or 1 items is already sorted
        return items
    middle = len(items) // 2
    return merge(merge_sort(items[:middle]), merge_sort(items[middle:]))


numbers = [random.randint(1, 100) for _ in range(15)]
print("Before:", numbers)
print("After: ", merge_sort(numbers))

import random


def quick_sort(items):
    if len(items) <= 1:
        return items
    pivot = random.choice(items)  # pick any item as the pivot
    smaller = [x for x in items if x < pivot]
    same = [x for x in items if x == pivot]
    bigger = [x for x in items if x > pivot]
    # sort each side, then glue them together
    return quick_sort(smaller) + same + quick_sort(bigger)

scripts.about: Writes bubble sort, selection sort and insertion sort by hand and checks them against sorted().
scripts.code:
import random


def bubble_sort(items):
    items = items[:]  # work on a copy
    for end in range(len(items) - 1, 0, -1):
        for i in range(end):
            if items[i] > items[i + 1]:  # bigger one "bubbles" to the right
                items[i], items[i + 1] = items[i + 1], items[i]
    return items


def selection_sort(items):
    items = items[:]
    for i in range(len(items)):
        smallest = i
        for j in range(i + 1, len(items)):  # find the smallest in the rest
            if items[j] < items[smallest]:
                smallest = j
        items[i], items[smallest] = items[smallest], items[i]
    return items


def insertion_sort(items):
    items = items[:]
    for i in range(1, len(items)):
        current = items[i]
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 and items[j] > current:  # slide bigger ones right
            items[j + 1] = items[j]
            j -= 1
        items[j + 1] = current
    return items


numbers = [random.randint(1, 99) for _ in range(12)]
print("Start:     ", numbers)
print("Bubble:    ", bubble_sort(numbers))
print("Selection: ", selection_sort(numbers))
print("Insertion: ", insertion_sort(numbers))

# Test them on 100 random lists to be sure they work
for _ in range(100):
    data = [random.randint(-50, 50) for _ in range(random.randint(0, 20))]
    assert bubble_sort(data) == selection_sort(data) == insertion_sort(data) == sorted(data)
print("All three passed 100 tests!")

moves = []


def hanoi(disks, start, helper, goal):
    """Move a pile of disks from start to goal, using helper as the spare peg."""
    if disks == 0:
        return
    hanoi(disks - 1, start, goal, helper)   # 1. move the smaller pile out of the way
    moves.append((disks, start, goal))      # 2. move the biggest disk
    hanoi(disks - 1, helper, start, goal)   # 3. put the smaller pile back on top

    print(f"Move {number}: disk {disk} from {start} to {goal}")

print(f"\nSolved {count} disks in {len(moves)} moves. The fewest possible is 2^{count} - 1 = {2 ** count - 1}.")

scripts.code:
WIDTH, HEIGHT = 78, 32
CHARS = " .:-=+*#%@"   # from "escaped fast" to "never escaped"
MAX_STEPS = 60

for row in range(HEIGHT):
    line = ""
    for col in range(WIDTH):
        # Turn this character's position into a complex number c
        c = complex(-2.2 + col * 3.0 / WIDTH, -1.2 + row * 2.4 / HEIGHT)
        z = 0j
        steps = 0
        # Keep doing z = z*z + c. If z flies far away, c is NOT in the set.
        while abs(z) <= 2 and steps < MAX_STEPS:
            z = z * z + c
            steps += 1
        line += CHARS[min(steps * len(CHARS) // MAX_STEPS, len(CHARS) - 1)]
    print(line)

print("The @ shape in the middle is the Mandelbrot set. Its edge is infinitely detailed!")

scripts.code:
import random
import tkinter as tk

WIDTH, HEIGHT = 600, 400
COLORS = ["tomato", "gold", "lime green", "deep sky blue", "orchid", "orange"]

window = tk.Tk()
window.title("Bouncing Shapes (click to add)")
canvas = tk.Canvas(window, width=WIDTH, height=HEIGHT, bg="black")
canvas.pack()
balls = []  # each ball is [canvas id, dx, dy]


def add_ball(x, y):
    r = random.randint(10, 30)
    shape = canvas.create_oval(x - r, y - r, x + r, y + r, fill=random.choice(COLORS), outline="")
    balls.append([shape, random.choice([-1, 1]) * random.uniform(2, 6), random.choice([-1, 1]) * random.uniform(2, 6)])


def animate():
    for ball in balls:
        shape, dx, dy = ball
        canvas.move(shape, dx, dy)
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = canvas.coords(shape)  # where the ball's box is now
        if x1 <= 0 or x2 >= WIDTH:
            ball[1] = -dx
        if y1 <= 0 or y2 >= HEIGHT:
            ball[2] = -dy
    window.after(16, animate)  # about 60 frames per second


canvas.bind("<Button-1>", lambda event: add_ball(event.x, event.y))
for _ in range(5):
    add_ball(random.randint(50, WIDTH - 50), random.randint(50, HEIGHT - 50))
animate()
window.mainloop()

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import colorchooser

window = tk.Tk()
window.title("Paint")
state = {"color": "black", "size": 6, "last": None}

canvas = tk.Canvas(window, width=700, height=480, bg="white", cursor="crosshair")
canvas.pack()


def paint(event):
    if state["last"]:
        x, y = state["last"]
        # Draw a line from the last spot to this one so fast strokes have no gaps
        canvas.create_line(x, y, event.x, event.y, fill=state["color"], width=state["size"],
                           capstyle=tk.ROUND, smooth=True)
    state["last"] = (event.x, event.y)


def stop(event):
    state["last"] = None


def pick_color():
    chosen = colorchooser.askcolor(color=state["color"])[1]  # [1] is the color as "#rrggbb"
    if chosen:
        state["color"] = chosen


def set_size(value):
    state["size"] = int(value)


canvas.bind("<B1-Motion>", paint)          # B1 = left mouse button held down
canvas.bind("<ButtonRelease-1>", stop)

bar = tk.Frame(window)
bar.pack(fill="x", pady=4)
for color in ["black", "red", "orange", "gold", "green", "blue", "purple", "white"]:
    tk.Button(bar, bg=color, width=2, command=lambda c=color: state.update(color=c)).pack(side="left", padx=2)
tk.Button(bar, text="More colors", command=pick_color).pack(side="left", padx=6)
size = tk.Scale(bar, from_=1, to=40, orient="horizontal", label="Brush", command=set_size)
size.set(state["size"])
size.pack(side="left", padx=6)
tk.Button(bar, text="Clear", command=lambda: canvas.delete("all")).pack(side="right", padx=6)
window.mainloop()

        t.dot(6)

scripts.about: Builds a random maze with a depth-first search, then draws it with turtle graphics.
scripts.code:
import random
import turtle

COLS, ROWS, CELL = 20, 15, 30
# walls[(c, r)] holds which sides of a cell still have walls
walls = {(c, r): {"N", "S", "E", "W"} for c in range(COLS) for r in range(ROWS)}
MOVES = {"N": (0, 1, "S"), "S": (0, -1, "N"), "E": (1, 0, "W"), "W": (-1, 0, "E")}

# Depth-first search: walk to random unvisited neighbors, back up when stuck
stack = [(0, 0)]
visited = {(0, 0)}
while stack:
    c, r = stack[-1]
    options = [(d, (c + dc, r + dr), opposite) for d, (dc, dr, opposite) in MOVES.items()
               if (c + dc, r + dr) in walls and (c + dc, r + dr) not in visited]
    if not options:
        stack.pop()
        continue
    direction, nxt, opposite = random.choice(options)
    walls[(c, r)].discard(direction)   # knock down the wall between the two cells
    walls[nxt].discard(opposite)
    visited.add(nxt)
    stack.append(nxt)
walls[(0, 0)].discard("W")                 # entrance
walls[(COLS - 1, ROWS - 1)].discard("E")   # exit

screen = turtle.Screen()
screen.tracer(0)
t = turtle.Turtle()
t.hideturtle()
t.width(3)
left, bottom = -COLS * CELL / 2, -ROWS * CELL / 2


def line(x1, y1, x2, y2):
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x1, y1)
    t.pendown()
    t.goto(x2, y2)


for (c, r), sides in walls.items():
    x, y = left + c * CELL, bottom + r * CELL
    if "S" in sides:
        line(x, y, x + CELL, y)
    if "N" in sides:
        line(x, y + CELL, x + CELL, y + CELL)
    if "W" in sides:
        line(x, y, x, y + CELL)
    if "E" in sides:
        line(x + CELL, y, x + CELL, y + CELL)

screen.update()
turtle.done()

scripts.about: Draws a Sierpinski triangle: a triangle made of three smaller triangles, made of smaller triangles, and so on.
scripts.code:
import turtle

COLORS = ["midnight blue", "blue", "dodger blue", "deep sky blue", "light sky blue", "white"]


def triangle(t, points, color):
    t.fillcolor(color)
    t.penup()
    t.goto(points[0])
    t.pendown()
    t.begin_fill()
    t.goto(points[1])
    t.goto(points[2])
    t.goto(points[0])
    t.end_fill()


def middle(a, b):
    return ((a[0] + b[0]) / 2, (a[1] + b[1]) / 2)


def sierpinski(t, points, depth):
    triangle(t, points, COLORS[depth % len(COLORS)])
    if depth > 0:
        a, b, c = points
        sierpinski(t, [a, middle(a, b), middle(a, c)], depth - 1)
        sierpinski(t, [b, middle(a, b), middle(b, c)], depth - 1)
        sierpinski(t, [c, middle(c, b), middle(a, c)], depth - 1)


screen = turtle.Screen()
screen.tracer(0)
t = turtle.Turtle()
t.hideturtle()
sierpinski(t, [(-300, -250), (0, 270), (300, -250)], 5)
screen.update()
turtle.done()

scripts.about: Draws spirograph patterns using the math of a small wheel rolling inside a big one.
scripts.code:
import math
import turtle

R, r, d = 200, 73, 110   # big wheel, small wheel, pen distance from the small wheel's center

screen = turtle.Screen()
screen.bgcolor("black")
screen.colormode(255)
screen.tracer(0)
t = turtle.Turtle()
t.hideturtle()
t.width(2)


def point(angle):
    """Where the pen is after the small wheel has rolled 'angle' radians."""
    x = (R - r) * math.cos(angle) + d * math.cos((R - r) / r * angle)
    y = (R - r) * math.sin(angle) - d * math.sin((R - r) / r * angle)
    return x, y


# The pattern repeats after r / gcd(R, r) trips around
turns = r // math.gcd(R, r)
steps = 3000
t.penup()
t.goto(point(0))
t.pendown()
for i in range(1, steps + 1):
    angle = i / steps * turns * 2 * math.pi
    shade = int(127 + 127 * math.sin(i / 200))
    t.color(255, shade, 255 - shade)
    t.goto(point(angle))
    if i % 100 == 0:
        screen.update()

screen.update()
turtle.done()

        rows = db.execute("SELECT id, name, phone, email FROM contacts WHERE name LIKE ? ORDER BY name",
                          (f"%{word}%",)).fetchall()

import csv
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path

SAMPLE = "name,age,city\nStorm,12,Denver\nNova,13,Austin\n"


def smart(value):
    """Turn '12' into 12 and '3.5' into 3.5, but leave words as words."""
    for kind in (int, float):
        try:
            return kind(value)
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return value


name = input("CSV file (Enter for a sample): ").strip()

    target = source.with_suffix(".json")

    target = Path(__file__).with_name("sample.json")

rows = [{key: smart(value) for key, value in row.items()} for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))]
target.write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
print(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))
print(f"\nSaved {len(rows)} records to {target}")

import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

SAMPLE = [
    {"name": "Sword", "damage": 12, "rarity": "rare"},
    {"name": "Bow", "damage": 8, "range": 30},
    {"name": "Potion", "heal": 25},
]

    target = source.with_suffix(".csv")
else:

if not isinstance(data, list) or not all(isinstance(item, dict) for item in data):
    raise SystemExit("The JSON needs to be a list of objects, like [{...}, {...}].")

# Collect every key that appears anywhere, keeping the order we first see them
columns = []
for item in data:
    for key in item:
        if key not in columns:
            columns.append(key)

with open(target, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=columns, restval="")  # missing values become empty cells

    writer.writerows(data)

import csv

Uranus,28,51118,17.2,19.2
Neptune,16,49528,16.1,30.06
"""

for row in rows:  # turn number columns into numbers
    for key in ("moons", "diameter_km", "day_hours", "distance_au"):

scripts.about: A small module any game can import to save scores in a database and get the top 10.
scripts.code:
import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

DB_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("highscores.db")


def _connect():
    db = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores (name TEXT, score INTEGER, game TEXT, played TEXT)")
    return db


def add(name, score, game="default"):
    """Save one score."""
    with _connect() as db:  # 'with' commits the changes for us
        db.execute("INSERT INTO scores VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                   (name, int(score), game, datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")))


def top(game="default", limit=10):
    """Return the best scores as a list of (name, score)."""
    with _connect() as db:
        return db.execute("SELECT name, score FROM scores WHERE game = ? ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT ?",
                          (game, limit)).fetchall()


def best_for(name, game="default"):
    with _connect() as db:
        row = db.execute("SELECT MAX(score) FROM scores WHERE name = ? AND game = ?", (name, game)).fetchone()
        return row[0] or 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import random
    for player in ["Storm", "Doodle", "Nova"]:
        add(player, random.randint(100, 1000), game="demo")
    print("Top scores for the demo game:")
    for rank, (name, score) in enumerate(top("demo"), start=1):
        print(f"  {rank}. {name:<8} {score}")
    print("Storm's best:", best_for("Storm", "demo"))

import csv
from pathlib import Path

folder = Path(input("Folder with CSV files: ").strip() or ".").expanduser()
files = sorted(p for p in folder.glob("*.csv") if p.name != "merged.csv")
if not files:
    raise SystemExit("No .csv files found there.")

all_rows = []
columns = ["source_file"]
for path in files:
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for column in reader.fieldnames or []:
            if column not in columns:
                columns.append(column)
        for row in reader:
            row["source_file"] = path.name
            all_rows.append(row)
    print(f"Read {path.name}")

out = folder / "merged.csv"
with open(out, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=columns, restval="")
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(all_rows)

print(f"\nMerged {len(all_rows)} rows from {len(files)} files into {out}")
print("Columns:", ", ".join(columns))

scripts.code:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

XML = """
<library>
  <book id="1" year="1997">
    <title>Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone</title>
    <author>J.K. Rowling</author>
    <pages>223</pages>
  </book>
  <book id="2" year="1937">
    <title>The Hobbit</title>
    <author>J.R.R. Tolkien</author>
    <pages>310</pages>
  </book>
  <book id="3" year="2008">
    <title>The Hunger Games</title>
    <author>Suzanne Collins</author>
    <pages>374</pages>
  </book>
</library>
"""

root = ET.fromstring(XML)
print("The root tag is:", root.tag)

for book in root.findall("book"):
    title = book.find("title").text
    author = book.findtext("author")
    pages = int(book.findtext("pages"))
    year = book.get("year")  # attributes are inside the tag itself
    print(f"{title} by {author} ({year}), {pages} pages")

total = sum(int(b.findtext("pages")) for b in root.iter("book"))
print("Total pages:", total)

# You can also build XML and turn it back into text
new = ET.SubElement(root, "book", id="4", year="2026")
ET.SubElement(new, "title").text = "My First Python Book"
print("\nNew book added:", ET.tostring(new, encoding="unicode"))
